label: token right after an early "a" (original position 1 or 2)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at step 1 or 2 when the previous input token was "a", whatever the current token is. Magnitude is largest at t=1, when "a" is the first token (top examples reach about 0.97-1.0 of max). It is weaker at t=2, when "a" is the second token (about 0.5-0.75 of max). It does not fire after an "a" at position 2 or later (t>=3 is only a trace), and it does not fire on the delimiter or in the copy phase. Missed activations hold about 0% of the mass: tiny activations after a first-token "j", and t=3 after "aa". It has no false positives on dev.

issues: I reproduced the test scores: precision 1.0, recall 0.977, F1 0.989, mass recall 0.9997, correlation 0.976. There were 0 false positives on either dev or test.

The magnitude claim holds. With t==1 the predicate covers the top two activation quartiles (0.95 and 1.0). With t==2 it covers the bottom two (0.91 and 1.0). So the strongest activations are when 'a' is the first token, and they are weaker when 'a' is the second token.

Missed activations carry 0.0% of the mass and come in two near-zero classes. The first is t=1 after a first-token 'j', specifically 'j t' at about 0.00. The second is t=3 after an 'a' at position 2, at about 0.02-0.11, including the 'aa' case. The explanation describes the t=3 class as 'after aa', but it also shows up after other tokens followed by 'a' (e.g. 'z o a p'). This is a minor imprecision with no effect on the scores.
Delimiter activations are 0. The copy phase has 19 of 2.7M steps active, with mass share 5e-5, so it is effectively silent there.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
